title: Screen Time in the Early Years: Guidance by Age
summary: According to the American Academy of Pediatrics’ (AAP) 2016 statement, screen media should be avoided before 18 months, except video chatting. At 18–24 months, parents who choose to introduce media should choose high-quality content and use it together with their child, avoiding solo viewing. From ages two to five, the statement limits screen use to one hour daily of high-quality content with co-viewing. WHO’s 2019 guidelines do not recommend sedentary screen time for infants or one-year-olds, and limit it to one hour daily at age two; less is better. The recommendations differ at 18–24 months; they do not establish one shared rule of zero screens under two. Make time for sensory play, movement, reading and direct interaction with your child; screens should not replace these activities or sleep.
try_this: This week: Try a 'zero screens hour' daily—put the phone in another room, get down on the floor with your child, and play together with anything available (plastic containers, pots, cloth balls). Notice: Does he interact more? Does he sleep better? Record your observations.
reflection_prompts: What is the hardest moment in your day when you tend to hand your child a screen? What is a possible alternative?
Have you noticed a difference in your child’s behavior after a screen-free day?
